results.name: Marc DeBevoise Named OverDrive CEO as Founder Steve Potash Steps Into Chairman Role | Printed Word Reviews
results.content:
# Marc DeBevoise Named OverDrive CEO as Founder Steve Potash Steps Into Chairman Role  
June 23, 2026 at 11:30:27 AM  
OverDrive, the digital publishing giant that powers e-book and audiobook access for libraries and schools worldwide, is entering a new era. The company announced Tuesday that veteran media and technology executive Marc DeBevoise has been appointed Chief Executive Officer.  
DeBevoise succeeds company founder Steve Potash, who is transitioning to Chairman of the Board after 40 years leading the organization.  
The leadership change represents a carefully planned succession strategy designed to scale OverDrive's digital platform and accelerate its international footprint. Potash, who founded the company four decades ago, successfully guided OverDrive from the early days of digital content experimentation into a global infrastructure mainstay. Today, the platform serves educational and public institutions in more than 115 countries.  
DeBevoise is well-equipped for the expansion push, bringing a heavyweight corporate resume to the chief executive suite. Before joining OverDrive as President, where he worked directly alongside Potash to map out the company's future, DeBevoise served as the CEO of Brightcove, Chief Digital Officer of Paramount, and CEO of CBS Interactive.
The transition has earned strong backing from OverDrive’s primary institutional investors. Richard Sarnoff, Chairman of Media for KKR Americas Private Equity, emphasized that DeBevoise’s operational experience makes him the right fit for the company's next chapter.  
"Steve built an extraordinary organization — a mission-driven company with true global impact — and Marc is the ideal leader to write its next chapter," Sarnoff said. "Marc's vision, energy, and operational depth give us every confidence that his leadership will not only augment its success as a business but also heighten its outstanding record of service."  
For Potash, the move marks a significant personal milestone, though not an exit from the company he built from scratch.  
"Founding and building OverDrive has been the most rewarding journey of my career," Potash said, adding that the company is uniquely positioned for evolution. As Chairman, Potash intends to maintain an active role in supporting DeBevoise's executive team while continuing to champion the libraries and schools at the core of OverDrive's mission.  
Moving forward, DeBevoise’s mandate will focus on expanding global content access, growing the platform’s infrastructure, and capturing a broader audience of digital readers and learners.  
"OverDrive has extraordinary reach, incredible momentum, and an enduring mission — and I’m thrilled to lead this company forward," DeBevoise said.  
*Reported by Printed Word Reviews*

Mar 04, 2026 · Digital content provider OverDrive announced on March 3 that it has brought in Marc DeBevoise as its new president. DeBevoise, former CEO at the video platform Brightcove and a past leader at the online content network CBS Interactive, will help guide the company known for library reading app Libby, school “science of reading app” Sora, and video-streaming app Kanopy.
OverDrive founder and CEO Steve Potash, who served as company president prior to DeBevoise’s appointment, said in a statement that he expects DeBevoise to “make Libby, Sora, and Kanopy even more user friendly, more inclusive, and more joyful to use” and “help libraries and schools do what they do best, change lives through reading, viewing, and learning.” Potash and DeBevoise now will work together with the OverDrive leadership team.

results.name: OverDrive Founder Steve Potash Steps Back; Marc DeBevoise Takes Over as CEO
results.content:
# OverDrive Founder Steve Potash Steps Back; Marc DeBevoise Takes Over as CEO  
It's the end of an era at OverDrive. On June 23, the company announced that founder Steve Potash has stepped back from his role as CEO, handing the reins to Marc DeBevoise, who joined the company roughly four months ago as President.  
It's the end of an era at OverDrive. On June 23, the company announced that the company's founder Steve Potash has stepped back from his role as CEO, handing the reins to Marc DeBevoise, [who joined the company roughly four months ago as President](https://www.wordsandmoney.com/overdrive-names-marc-debevoise-president/).  
In a release, OverDrive reps said Potash will stay on as Chairman of the Board, “ensuring a smooth transition” and “continuing to advance the company's mission to expand access to reading and learning.” According to the release, the leadership change was part of “a planned succession.”
"Steve built an extraordinary organization—a mission-driven company with true global impact—and Marc is the ideal leader to write its next chapter," said Richard Sarnoff, Chairman of Media, KKR Americas Private Equity, [which acquired OverDrive from Rakuten Kobo in 2020](https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/industry-deals/article/83551-kkr-completes-overdrive-purchase.html?ref=wordsandmoney.com). "Marc's vision, energy, and operational depth give us every confidence that his leadership will not only augment its success as a business but also heighten its outstanding record of service to libraries and their patrons, to schools and their students, and to publishers and content owners."  
In a statement, Potash said building OverDrive was the most “rewarding journey” of his career, and said he looked forward to “continuing to champion the libraries, schools, and institutions at the heart of our mission."  
DeBevoise, meanwhile, said that he was “thrilled” to lead OverDrive’s next chapter.  
"OverDrive has extraordinary reach, incredible momentum, and an enduring mission—and I’m thrilled to lead this company forward," DeBevoise said. "I'm grateful to Steve for his continued partnership and to the Board for their confidence, and I look forward to working with our team and partners to build on everything this company stands for."
The move comes just days ahead of the 2026 American Library Association Annual Conference, set to run from June 25-30 in Chicago, and as the library ebook market has entered a contentious new period, with several states and municipalities considering—and three so far passing—legislation designed to rein in what librarians say are unsustainable prices and license terms from the major publishers.  
Potash has come out strongly against the current wave of library ebook legislation,—and last fall rankled librarians with [a 54-page submission](https://www.wordsandmoney.com/content/files/2026/01/Testimony-of-Steve-Potash--OverDrive-V1.1_1.6.26.pdf) that railed against Washington D.C.’s library ebook bill. [The D.C. bill was signed into law on May 28.](https://www.wordsandmoney.com/district-of-columbias-library-ebook-bill-is-signed-into-law/)  
Potash’s enduring legacy, however, will be as a historic innovator, a staunch library supporter, and, with his wife Loree, a generous philanthropist.  
[According to Hallie Rich at Library Journal](https://www.libraryjournal.com/story/news/overdrive-ceo-transitions-to-new-role?ref=wordsandmoney.com), a “central component” of Potash's future will be the development of the “OverDrive Foundation,” which Rich reports will “support initiatives that strengthen literacy outcomes, advance library services, and promote learning across all stages of life.”

results.content:
After serving as CEO of OverDrive for 40 years, Potash is transitioning to the role of board chairman and DeBevoise, a longtime senior executive in the streaming technology space, is taking over after spending the last three-plus months as the company’s first-ever president.
Jul 13, 2026 · Posted 4 hrs ago at 3: 00 PM · Facebook · Twitter · WhatsApp · SMS · Email · +1 · DeBevoise · +1 · Potash · Facebook · Twitter · WhatsApp · SMS · Email · Print · Copy article link · Save · OverDrive founder Steve Potash compared Marc DeBevoise, the company’s new CEO, to a certain space ranger currently on the big screen in theaters around the world.
After serving as CEO of OverDrive for 40 years, Potash is transitioning to the role of board chairman and DeBevoise, a longtime senior executive in the streaming technology space, is taking over after spending the last three-plus months as the company’s first-ever president.
OverDrive announced the transition in a news release June 23. “I’ve been in that combined industry of media and tech, and really my career for the past 25 years has been about evolving access to content,” DeBevoise, who previously held senior executive roles for CBS and ViacomCBS, which is now Paramount Global, and was the CEO of Brightcove Inc., a video hosting and streaming technology platform from March 2022 to February 2025, when it was acquired by Bending Spoons, an Italian technology company, told the CJN.
New York City-based private equity firm KKR & Co., purchased a controlling stake in OverDrive in June 2020 and Potash, 73, said in the last few years, conversations were had during board meetings with KKR in the last handful of years about a succession plan. “About two years ago, we started a national search for a CEO successor,” Potash said.
